seo.title: HTS Chapter 85 Tariffs 2026: Electronics, Semiconductor, Battery & Solar Import Duty Rates | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: Searchable U.S. duty table for all 982 HTS Chapter 85 lines: smartphones, chips, lithium-ion batteries, solar cells, motors, transformers, TVs, cable. Section 301 China rates (50% chips and solar), 2026 Section 301, Section 232 auto parts and metals, Canada 50%.

overview.intro:
Chapter 85 covers electrical machinery and electronics: motors, generators, wind turbines and transformers (8501–8504); batteries (8506–8507); household and personal appliances (8508–8516); smartphones, network gear, audio, cameras, radios and TVs (8517–8529); switching and control apparatus, capacitors, resistors and printed circuits (8530–8538); lamps and LEDs, semiconductors, solar cells and chips (8539–8542); and other electrical apparatus, wire and cable, electrodes, insulators and e-waste (8543–8549). Base rates are low: **566 of 982 lines are Free** and the rest pay 1.3% to 15%.

What decides the cost is the extra duty, which depends on the country and the product:

- **China:** Section 301 covers 901 lines: 25% (Lists 1–3) or 7.5% (List 4A), **50% on semiconductors, chips and solar cells** (U.S. note 31), and **25% on lithium-ion batteries and permanent magnets** since January 1, 2026. Most lines also pay the 12.5% 2026 Section 301 duty. Smartphones (8517.13) are on no China list and are exempt from the 2026 duty, so they enter **Free**.
- **60 other economies:** the 2026 Section 301 actions add 10% or 12.5% (the EU, Japan, Korea and Taiwan pay a 10%–15% floor instead) on 909 lines. Smartphones, switches and routers (8517.62), SSDs, display modules, computer monitors, semiconductors and chips are exempt (note 52(b), 73 lines); solar cells are not. USMCA goods of Canada and Mexico are exempt.
- **Section 232:** 85 lines (motors, lithium-ion and lead-acid batteries, ignition and lighting parts, car radios, wiring sets) pay 25% when they are parts of cars or light trucks (15% in total for the EU, Japan, Korea and Taiwan) and 25% when they are truck or bus parts; 68 metal-heavy lines (transformers, wind turbines, insulated copper and aluminum cable) pay 25% of their full value and 15 a 15% floor; drone docking stations pay 100%.
- **Canada:** 62 lines (smartphones, network gear, TVs, cameras, printed circuits) pay **50% under Section 338** since August 22, 2026, even with a USMCA claim.

Two things that do **not** apply: the Section 232 semiconductor duty (Proclamation 11002, U.S. note 39) reaches only advanced chips in computers and computer parts of 8471.50, 8471.80 and 8473.30, not chips imported on their own; and the Section 201 solar safeguard ended on February 6, 2026. A new Section 232 duty of 15% plus minimum import prices on solar cells and modules starts December 4, 2026. Antidumping and countervailing duties on solar cells, aluminum wire and cable, large power transformers and graphite electrodes come on top; they are company-specific and not in this table.

productGroups.label: Electric motors and generators
productGroups.blurb: Electric motors of every size (AC, DC, universal, brushless, EV traction motors), generators and photovoltaic DC generators: 71 lines, Free to 6.7%. China Section 301: 25% on 71; Section 232 auto parts on 32 when they are car or light-truck parts; truck and bus parts on 28; Section 232 metals 25% on 4.

productGroups.label: Generating sets and rotary converters
productGroups.blurb: Diesel and gas generating sets, wind-powered generating sets (wind turbines) and rotary converters: 12 lines, 2% to 3%. China Section 301: 25% on 12; Section 232 metals 25% on 5.

productGroups.label: Parts of motors and generators
productGroups.blurb: Parts for the motors and generators of 8501 and 8502: stators, rotors, wind-turbine nacelle parts, laminations: 11 lines, Free to 6.5%. China Section 301: 25% on 11; Section 232 metals 25% on 8.

productGroups.label: Transformers, power supplies and inductors
productGroups.blurb: Transformers (distribution and large power transformers), ballasts, static converters (power supplies, inverters, chargers, rectifiers) and inductors, with parts: 54 lines, Free to 6.6%. China Section 301: 25% on 53, 7.5% on 1; Section 232 metals 25% on 17; a 15% Section 232 floor on 12; drone docking stations 100% on 1.

productGroups.label: Magnets and electromagnetic devices
productGroups.blurb: Permanent magnets (including sintered neodymium-iron-boron rare-earth magnets), electromagnets, magnetic chucks and couplings, lifting heads: 13 lines, Free to 4.9%. China Section 301: 25% on 13; 1 exempt from the 2026 Section 301 duties.

productGroups.label: Primary cells and batteries
productGroups.blurb: Non-rechargeable cells and batteries: alkaline, lithium primary, silver-oxide, zinc-air and button cells: 14 lines, 2.7%. China Section 301: 25% on 14.

productGroups.label: Storage batteries (lithium-ion, lead-acid)
productGroups.blurb: Rechargeable batteries and parts: lithium-ion cells and packs (EV and other), lead-acid starter and industrial batteries, nickel-metal hydride and other chemistries, separators: 19 lines, 2.5% to 3.5%. China Section 301: 25% on 17, 7.5% on 2; Section 232 auto parts on 8 when they are car or light-truck parts; truck and bus parts on 4.

productGroups.label: Vacuum cleaners
productGroups.blurb: Vacuum cleaners with a self-contained motor (robot, stick and canister vacuums) and their parts: 4 lines, Free. China Section 301: 25% on 4; Section 232 metals 25% on 1; Canada +50% (Section 338) on 1.

productGroups.label: Domestic appliances with motor
productGroups.blurb: Food processors, blenders, juicers, mixers, garbage disposals and other domestic electromechanical appliances with a self-contained motor: 16 lines, Free to 4.2%. China Section 301: 25% on 5 (none on 11); Section 232 metals 25% on 1.

productGroups.label: Shavers and hair clippers
productGroups.blurb: Electric shavers, hair clippers and hair-removing appliances, with parts: 9 lines, Free to 4.2%. China Section 301: 25% on 7, 7.5% on 1 (none on 1).

productGroups.label: Ignition and starting equipment
productGroups.blurb: Spark plugs, ignition coils and magnetos, starter motors, alternators and other ignition or starting equipment for engines: 13 lines, Free to 3.1%. China Section 301: 25% on 13; Section 232 auto parts on 10 when they are car or light-truck parts; truck and bus parts on 10.

productGroups.label: Vehicle lighting and signaling
productGroups.blurb: Lighting and signaling equipment for bicycles and motor vehicles (headlamps, tail lamps), windshield wipers, defrosters and demisters: 16 lines, Free to 2.7%. China Section 301: 25% on 14, 7.5% on 2; Section 232 auto parts on 12 when they are car or light-truck parts; truck and bus parts on 12.

productGroups.label: Portable electric lamps
productGroups.blurb: Portable lamps with their own energy source: flashlights, headlamps and miners' safety lamps: 4 lines, 3.5% to 12.5%. China Section 301: 25% on 2 (none on 2); Section 232 metals 25% on 1.

productGroups.label: Industrial electric furnaces
productGroups.blurb: Industrial and laboratory electric furnaces and ovens (resistance, induction, dielectric), microwave and infrared heating equipment: 14 lines, Free to 4.2%. China Section 301: 25% on 14; Section 232 metals 25% on 2.

productGroups.label: Welding and soldering equipment
productGroups.blurb: Electric, laser, ultrasonic and electron-beam welding, brazing, soldering and cutting machines and parts: 12 lines, Free to 2.5%. China Section 301: 25% on 12; Section 232 metals 25% on 1.

productGroups.label: Water heaters, space heaters and household heating appliances
productGroups.blurb: Electric water heaters, space and soil heaters, hair dryers and irons, microwave ovens, cooking ranges, toasters, coffee makers, heating resistors: 43 lines, Free to 5.3%. China Section 301: 25% on 25, 7.5% on 7 (none on 11); Section 232 metals 25% on 9; a 15% Section 232 floor on 3.

productGroups.label: Smartphones and network equipment
productGroups.blurb: Telephone sets including smartphones, base stations, routers, switches, modems and other apparatus for voice, image or data networks, and parts: 15 lines, Free. China Section 301: 25% on 3, 7.5% on 5 (none on 7); 4 exempt from the 2026 Section 301 duties; Section 232 metals 25% on 1; Canada +50% (Section 338) on 6.

productGroups.label: Microphones, speakers and headphones
productGroups.blurb: Microphones, loudspeakers, headphones and earphones, audio-frequency amplifiers and sound amplifier sets: 16 lines, Free. China Section 301: 25% on 8, 7.5% on 6 (none on 2).

productGroups.label: Sound recording and reproducing apparatus
productGroups.blurb: Turntables, CD players, digital audio players, dictation machines, answering machines and other sound recorders: 15 lines, Free to 3.9%. China Section 301: 25% on 2, 7.5% on 5 (none on 8); Section 232 auto parts on 1 when they are car or light-truck parts; truck and bus parts on 1.

productGroups.label: Video recorders and players
productGroups.blurb: Video recording or reproducing apparatus such as Blu-ray and DVD players and digital video recorders: 4 lines, Free. China Section 301: 7.5% on 4; Canada +50% (Section 338) on 1.

productGroups.label: Parts of sound and video apparatus
productGroups.blurb: Parts and accessories of the apparatus of 8519 to 8521 (pickup cartridges, needles): 9 lines, Free to 3.9%. China Section 301: 25% on 9.

productGroups.label: Storage media: SSDs, cards, discs and tapes
productGroups.blurb: Solid-state storage (SSDs, flash drives, memory cards), smart cards, optical discs, magnetic tapes and cards, recorded or not: 25 lines, Free. China Section 301: 25% on 5, 7.5% on 20; 1 exempt from the 2026 Section 301 duties; Canada +50% (Section 338) on 5.

productGroups.label: Flat panel display modules
productGroups.blurb: Flat panel display modules (LCD, OLED), with or without touch screens, without drivers or with drivers: 8 lines, Free to 4.5%. China Section 301: 25% on 6, 7.5% on 2; all exempt from the 2026 Section 301 duties.

productGroups.label: Cameras and transmitters
productGroups.blurb: Radio and TV transmission apparatus, television cameras, digital cameras, video camera recorders, security and dash cameras: 21 lines, Free. China Section 301: 25% on 19, 7.5% on 1 (none on 1); Section 232 auto parts on 1 when they are car or light-truck parts; truck and bus parts on 1; Canada +50% (Section 338) on 11.

productGroups.label: Radar and navigation apparatus
productGroups.blurb: Radar apparatus, radio navigational aids (GPS receivers) and radio remote-control apparatus: 6 lines, Free. China Section 301: 25% on 5 (none on 1); Canada +50% (Section 338) on 5.

productGroups.label: Radio receivers
productGroups.blurb: Radio broadcast receivers: car radios and infotainment receivers, clock radios and portable radios: 27 lines, Free to 2%. China Section 301: 25% on 9, 7.5% on 3 (none on 15); Section 232 auto parts on 7 when they are car or light-truck parts; truck and bus parts on 7.

productGroups.label: Monitors, projectors and televisions
productGroups.blurb: Computer monitors, other monitors, projectors and television receivers (LCD, OLED and LED TVs): 79 lines, Free to 5%. China Section 301: 25% on 22, 7.5% on 51 (none on 6); 1 exempt from the 2026 Section 301 duties; Canada +50% (Section 338) on 6.

productGroups.label: Parts of TVs, radios, cameras and radar
productGroups.blurb: Parts for 8524 to 8528: antennas and reflectors, open-cell TV panels, tuners and other parts: 46 lines, Free. China Section 301: 25% on 45, 7.5% on 1; Section 232 metals 25% on 1; Canada +50% (Section 338) on 10.

productGroups.label: Railway and traffic signaling equipment
productGroups.blurb: Electrical signaling, safety and traffic control equipment for railways, roads, waterways, ports and airfields: 3 lines, Free. China Section 301: 25% on 3.

productGroups.label: Alarms, bells and indicator panels
productGroups.blurb: Electric sound or visual signaling apparatus: burglar and fire alarms, doorbells, LED and LCD indicator panels and signboards: 16 lines, Free to 1.3%. China Section 301: 25% on 10, 7.5% on 5 (none on 1).

productGroups.label: Capacitors
productGroups.blurb: Fixed, variable and adjustable electrical capacitors (ceramic, tantalum, aluminum electrolytic, film) and parts: 29 lines, Free. China Section 301: 25% on 29.

productGroups.label: Resistors
productGroups.blurb: Electrical resistors, rheostats and potentiometers (other than heating resistors) and parts: 25 lines, Free. China Section 301: 25% on 25.

productGroups.label: Printed circuits
productGroups.blurb: Bare printed circuit boards (PCBs), rigid and flexible, without components mounted: 7 lines, Free. China Section 301: 25% on 7; Canada +50% (Section 338) on 7.

productGroups.label: High-voltage switchgear (over 1,000 V)
productGroups.blurb: Fuses, circuit breakers, isolating switches, lightning arresters and other apparatus for circuits over 1,000 volts: 12 lines, 2% to 2.7%. China Section 301: 25% on 12.

productGroups.label: Switches, breakers, relays and connectors (1,000 V or less)
productGroups.blurb: Fuses, breakers, relays, switches, sockets, plugs, lamp holders, connectors and fiber-optic connectors for circuits of 1,000 volts or less: 43 lines, Free to 2.7%. China Section 301: 25% on 42, 7.5% on 1; Section 232 auto parts on 1 when they are car or light-truck parts; truck and bus parts on 1; Section 232 metals 25% on 1.

productGroups.label: Control panels and switchboards
productGroups.blurb: Boards, panels, consoles and cabinets with switching apparatus: switchboards, motor control centers, programmable controllers (PLCs): 10 lines, Free to 2.7%. China Section 301: 25% on 10; Section 232 auto parts on 10 when they are car or light-truck parts; drone docking stations 100% on 1; Canada +50% (Section 338) on 4.

productGroups.label: Parts of switching apparatus
productGroups.blurb: Parts for 8535 to 8537: unequipped panels and boxes, molded and other parts: 9 lines, Free to 3.5%. China Section 301: 25% on 9; Section 232 metals 25% on 1.

productGroups.label: Lamps and LED light sources
productGroups.blurb: Filament and discharge lamps, sealed-beam lamp units, UV and IR lamps, arc lamps, and LED light sources (LED bulbs and modules): 40 lines, Free to 5.8%. China Section 301: 25% on 22, 7.5% on 5 (none on 13); Section 232 auto parts on 2 when they are car or light-truck parts; truck and bus parts on 2.

productGroups.label: Electron tubes
productGroups.blurb: Thermionic, cold cathode and photocathode tubes: cathode-ray tubes, camera tubes, magnetrons, klystrons, microwave tubes: 38 lines, Free to 15%. China Section 301: 25% on 38.

productGroups.label: Semiconductor devices and solar cells
productGroups.blurb: Diodes, transistors, thyristors, LEDs, photosensitive devices, crystalline silicon solar cells and modules, piezoelectric crystals: 36 lines, Free. China Section 301: 50% on 29, 25% on 7; 26 exempt from the 2026 Section 301 duties.

productGroups.label: Integrated circuits (chips)
productGroups.blurb: Electronic integrated circuits: processors and controllers, memories (DRAM, NAND), amplifiers and other ICs, and parts: 31 lines, Free. China Section 301: 50% on 31; all exempt from the 2026 Section 301 duties.

productGroups.label: Other electrical machines and apparatus
productGroups.blurb: Particle accelerators, signal generators, electroplating machines, e-cigarettes and vaporizers, drone controllers, electric fence energizers and other apparatus not elsewhere specified: 33 lines, Free to 2.6%. China Section 301: 25% on 30, 7.5% on 1 (none on 2); Section 232 metals 25% on 1; Canada +50% (Section 338) on 3.

productGroups.label: Insulated wire and cable, fiber-optic cable
productGroups.blurb: Insulated winding wire, coaxial cable, ignition and vehicle wiring sets (harnesses), insulated conductors and power cable, fiber-optic cables: 19 lines, Free to 5.3%. China Section 301: 25% on 19; Section 232 auto parts on 1 when they are car or light-truck parts; truck and bus parts on 1; Section 232 metals 25% on 10; Canada +50% (Section 338) on 3.

productGroups.label: Carbon and graphite electrodes and brushes
productGroups.blurb: Carbon and graphite electrodes (for electric-arc furnaces), carbon brushes, lamp and battery carbons: 8 lines, Free. China Section 301: 25% on 8.

productGroups.label: Electrical insulators
productGroups.blurb: Electrical insulators of glass, ceramics or other materials: 5 lines, Free to 3%. China Section 301: 25% on 5.

productGroups.label: Insulating fittings and conduit
productGroups.blurb: Insulating fittings for electrical machines (ceramic or plastic), and electrical conduit tubing lined with insulating material: 7 lines, Free to 4.6%. China Section 301: 25% on 7; Section 232 metals 25% on 4.

productGroups.label: Electrical parts not elsewhere specified
productGroups.blurb: Electrical parts of machinery or apparatus not specified elsewhere in the chapter: 1 line, Free. China Section 301: 25% on 1.

productGroups.label: Electrical and electronic waste and scrap
productGroups.blurb: Waste and scrap of batteries and electrical and electronic assemblies (e-waste), including spent lead-acid batteries: 14 lines, Free. China Section 301: 25% on 6, 7.5% on 8; 1 exempt from the 2026 Section 301 duties.

workedExamples.title: Smartphones from China, India or Vietnam, and from Canada
workedExamples.body: Smartphones are **Free** under the general rate, are on none of the China Section 301 lists, and 8517.13 is on the 2026 Section 301 exemption list (note 52(b), 9903.05.86). So a $500,000 shipment from China, India or Vietnam owes **no duty**. The IEEPA duties that applied in 2025 ended on February 24, 2026. The exception is Canada: 8517.13 is on the Section 338 list (note 51(b)(3), 9903.03.14), so Canadian smartphones pay **50%** since August 22, 2026, USMCA claim or not.

workedExamples.title: Lithium-ion EV battery packs from China
workedExamples.body: **3.4%** base, **+25%** China Section 301 (note 31(g), 9903.91.06) and, as parts of passenger vehicles, **+25%** Section 232 (note 33(g), 9903.94.05): **53.4%**, or $534,000 on $1 million. The 12.5% 2026 Section 301 duty does not apply to Section 232 auto parts (note 52(f)(3)). A lithium-ion battery of 8507.60.00.90 used outside vehicles, for example in energy storage, enters under 9903.94.06 with no Section 232 duty and pays the 12.5% instead: **40.9%**.

workedExamples.title: Processors and controllers (8542.31) from China and from Taiwan
workedExamples.body: Chips are **Free** at base. Chinese chips pay **+50%** under Section 301 (note 31(f), 9903.91.05, since January 1, 2025); 8542 is exempt from the 2026 Section 301 duty. Chips from Taiwan, Malaysia, Korea or Vietnam pay **nothing**: 8542 is on the note 52(b) exemption list, and the 25% Section 232 semiconductor duty (9903.79.01) covers only certain advanced chips in computers of 8471.50, 8471.80 and 8473.30, not loose chips. A further Section 301 increase on Chinese semiconductors is set for June 23, 2027 at a rate USTR has not yet announced.

workedExamples.title: Solar modules from China, Vietnam or India
workedExamples.body: Modules are **Free** at base and are not on the note 52(b) list. Chinese modules pay **62.5%** (50% note 31(c), 9903.91.02, plus 12.5%) and the 2012 and 2015 AD/CVD orders; Vietnamese modules **12.5%** plus the June 2025 AD/CVD orders on Cambodia, Malaysia, Thailand and Vietnam; Indian modules **10%**; Commerce found dumping and subsidies on Indian, Indonesian and Lao cells and modules on September 16, 2026, and orders follow if the ITC finds injury. The Section 201 safeguard ended February 6, 2026. From December 4, 2026, Proclamation 11052 adds a 15% Section 232 duty and a minimum import price of $0.38 per watt for modules ($0.22 for cells).

workedExamples.title: Insulated copper cable from Mexico
workedExamples.body: **2.6%** base, Free with a USMCA claim. The cable is on the Section 232 copper list (note 16(c)(viii)), so it pays **+25% of its full value** (9903.82.09) whatever the FTA claim: **25%** with USMCA, 27.6% without. The 2026 Section 301 duty does not apply to Section 232 metals goods (note 52(f)(1)). Cable whose aluminum, steel and copper are under 15% of its weight enters under 9903.82.03 with no Section 232 duty.

workedExamples.title: Large power transformer from South Korea
workedExamples.body: Transformers over 10,000 kVA are on the note 16(c)(x) list of fixed industrial equipment, which pays a **15% floor** until December 31, 2027 (9903.82.10: the total is 15% when the base rate is lower). So a $5 million Korean transformer owes **$750,000** in tariff, KORUS or not. Large power transformers from Korea are also under a 2012 antidumping order, continued in 2024, with company-specific cash deposits on top. From January 1, 2028 the line moves to 25% on top of the base rate.

workedExamples.title: 65-inch LCD TV from Mexico or China
workedExamples.body: **3.9%** base. A USMCA-qualifying Mexican TV enters **Free**; without a USMCA claim it pays **13.9%** (3.9% + 10% under 9903.05.55). A Chinese TV pays **23.9%**: 3.9% + 7.5% List 4A + 12.5% 2026 Section 301.

notes.chapterNotes:
**Exclusions (note 1).** Electrically warmed blankets and clothing, glass of heading 7011, semiconductor-manufacturing machines of heading 8486, medical vacuum apparatus (9018) and electrically heated furniture are not in Chapter 85. **Note 2:** headings 8501–8504 do not cover goods of 8511, 8512, 8540, 8541 or 8542. **Note 3:** batteries of 8507 include ancillary components such as connectors, temperature control and circuit protection devices. **Note 4:** heading 8509 covers only domestic electromechanical appliances (most under 20 kg).

**Definitions.** *Smartphones* (note 5) are cellular phones with a mobile operating system that runs multiple applications. *Solid-state non-volatile storage devices* and *smart cards* are defined in note 6; *flat panel display modules* (note 7) are display screens designed to be built into other goods, and heading 8524 takes precedence over every other heading. *Printed circuits* (note 8) carry only printed elements. *LED light sources* (note 11) are LED modules and LED lamps of 8539. Note 12 defines *semiconductor devices* (including semiconductor-based sensors, actuators, resonators and oscillators) and *electronic integrated circuits* (monolithic, hybrid, multichip and multi-component ICs); headings 8541 and 8542 take precedence over every other heading except 8523.

**Subheading notes** define high-speed, radiation-hardened and night-vision cameras (8525.81–8525.83) and spent batteries (8549.11–8549.19).
notes.additionalUsNotes: **1.** For 8501 and 8503, 746 W equals 1 horsepower. **2.** Toasters of 8516.72 include toaster-ovens. **3.** For 8517 and 8525, *transceivers* combine a transmitter and receiver that cannot work simultaneously. **4–6, 9, 10.** Rules for classifying television subassemblies, picture tubes and front panel assemblies (8529.90, 8540). **7.** *High definition* means a 16:9 or wider screen showing more than 700 scanning lines. **8.** The video display diagonal is the longest straight line across the visible faceplate. **11.** Lists the machines whose parts qualify for 8538.90.10. Statistical notes define, among others, the crystalline silicon photovoltaic cells and modules reported under 8541.42.00.10 and 8541.43.00.10.

tariffUpdates.h1: HTS Chapter 85: Electrical Machinery & Electronics — Tariff Updates

seo.title: Electronics & Semiconductor Tariff Updates 2025–2026: Section 301, Section 232, Solar, Batteries (HTS Ch. 85) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: Every U.S. tariff change on HTS Chapter 85 goods with official citations: China Section 301 at 50% on chips and solar cells, 25% on lithium-ion batteries and magnets, the 2026 Section 301 actions, Section 232 auto parts and metals, Canada's Section 338 duty, the end of the IEEPA tariffs and the solar safeguard, and the solar AD/CVD orders.

tariffUpdates.intro:
This page compares two editions of the tariff schedule, the **2025 Basic Edition** (in force January 1, 2025) and the current **2026 Revision 21** (in force October 9, 2026), and lists every extra duty that reaches Chapter 85 today. Base rates did not move: the only changes are 21 new statistical lines (EV traction motors, power supplies, lithium-ion and lead-acid batteries, semiconductor devices, chips) at unchanged rates.

The extra duties changed a lot. In 2025 the IEEPA duties hit Chapter 85 goods from Canada, Mexico and China, and the reciprocal tariff hit most other countries, but smartphones, computers and monitors, display modules, semiconductors and chips were exempted from the reciprocal tariff (memorandum of April 11, 2025, retroactive to April 5). The IEEPA duties ended on **February 24, 2026**, and the Section 122 surcharge that replaced them expired on **July 23, 2026**. What applies now: China's Section 301 duties (50% on chips and solar cells since 2024–2025, 25% on lithium-ion batteries and permanent magnets since January 1, 2026), the **2026 Section 301 actions** on 60 economies (from July 24, 2026; electronics exemptions in note 52(b)), the Brazil Section 301 duty, **Section 232** on auto parts (from May 3, 2025), truck and bus parts (November 1, 2025), metal-heavy goods on the full value (April 6, 2026) and drone docking stations (September 3, 2026), and Canada's **Section 338** duty (August 22, 2026). The Section 201 solar safeguard ended on February 6, 2026; a Section 232 duty on solar cells and modules begins December 4, 2026.

Antidumping and countervailing duty orders cover solar cells and modules, aluminum wire and cable, large power transformers and small-diameter graphite electrodes. They are company-specific, listed below for reference, and **not included in the tariff calculator**.
tariffUpdates.scope: Chapter 99 measures that reach Chapter 85 from any country: China Section 301 (notes 20 and 31), the 2026 Section 301 actions on 60 economies and Brazil (notes 50 and 52), Section 232 automobile parts (note 33), medium- and heavy-duty vehicle parts (note 38), metals (note 16), aluminum from Russia (note 19) and unmanned aircraft systems (note 43), Canada Section 338 (note 51), Russia's rates in lieu of column 2 (note 30), the scheduled Nicaragua Section 301 duty (note 29), and the ended IEEPA, Section 122 and Section 201 (solar, note 18) duties. The Section 232 semiconductor duty (note 39) is covered because people ask about it, though no Chapter 85 line is in it. AD/CVD orders are listed for reference. For the rate each supplier pays, see Rates by country.

inEffect.before: +25% (Lists 1–3) or +7.5% (List 4A); +50% on solar cells; 25% on chips (List 1)
inEffect.now: +25% or +7.5% (lists); +50% chips, semiconductors and solar cells; +25% lithium-ion batteries and permanent magnets; plus +12.5% on most lines
inEffect.exemption: Lists 1–3 (25%) and 4A (7.5%) together cover 832 lines; note 31 moved semiconductors and chips (8541 except solar, 8542: 56 lines) to 50% (9903.91.05) on January 1, 2025, solar cells and modules (8541.42/.43) to 50% (9903.91.02) on September 27, 2024, lead-acid battery parts (8507.90.40) to 25% (9903.91.01), and lithium-ion batteries (8507.60) and permanent magnets (8505.11) to 25% (9903.91.06) on January 1, 2026. 81 lines are on no China list, including smartphones (8517.13), many appliances and audio players. The 12.5% 2026 duty (9903.05.31) applies on top except to the 73 note 52(b) lines (chips, semiconductors other than solar cells, smartphones, SSDs, display modules, monitors, NdFeB magnets) and to Section 232 goods (note 52(f)). USTR extended 178 exclusions (9903.88.69) through November 9, 2026; 26 Chapter 85 lines have one, for the products described. USTR confirmed on October 7, 2026 that the 2018 actions continue.

inEffect.country: Russia (and Belarus, Cuba, North Korea for metals)
inEffect.measure: Column 2 rates, 35% in lieu of column 2 (note 30), 200% on aluminum derivatives (note 19), metals and the 2026 Section 301 duty
inEffect.before: Column 2 rates and 35% in lieu of column 2 on note 30 lines
inEffect.now: Column 2 rate (or 35%) + 12.5% (2026 Section 301) + 200% on aluminum derivatives or 25% on steel and copper derivatives
inEffect.exemption: Russian goods pay the column 2 rates (since April 9, 2022) and 35% in their place on 18 note 30 lines (lamps, wiring sets, LEDs, some insulators). 50 lines that were aluminum derivatives pay 200% when Russian (9903.85.68). Belarus, Cuba and North Korea pay 25% on the metals lines (9903.82.12) on top of column 2.
inEffect.whatItMeans: Russian electrical goods are close to prohibited: column 2 rates of 25% to 35% plus 12.5%, and 200% on aluminum-heavy goods.

changes.title: No Chapter 85 base-rate changes
changes.detail: 961 of 982 Chapter 85 lines carry the same General, Special and Column 2 rates in the 2026 Revision 21 as in the 2025 Basic Edition. The other 21 are new statistical lines at unchanged rates: 8501.64.01.10/.35/.55 (AC generators), 8504.40.95.71–.79 (static converters), 8507.20.80.92 (lead-acid batteries), 8507.60.00.30/.90 (lithium-ion batteries other than for EVs), 8541.29.00.55/.65/.85 and 8541.90.00.10/.80 (transistors and parts), 8542.39.00.70/.90 (ICs) and 8543.30.90.10/.90.

changes.title: FCC closes the Covered List component loophole
changes.detail: FCC rules effective October 13, 2026 bar equipment authorization for devices containing logic-bearing hardware components made by Covered List entities (where the whole device would be barred), require full certification for modifications by those entities, and require online marketplaces to show the FCC ID. Radio-frequency devices without a valid authorization cannot be imported for sale (47 CFR 2.1204).

changes.title: China Section 301 actions continue during the second four-year review
changes.detail: USTR received requests to continue the 2018 actions, so they did not terminate on July 6 and August 23, 2026 and stay in effect, subject to changes from the review.

changes.title: Preliminary dumping findings on large graphite electrodes from China and India
changes.detail: Commerce preliminarily found dumping of large-diameter graphite electrodes (over 425 mm, 8545.11.00.20) from China and India, in investigations begun in March 2026 together with subsidy investigations. Final determinations and the ITC's injury vote are still to come.

changes.title: Commerce limits stockpiling of solar cells and modules before December 4
changes.detail: A temporary BIS rule (September 22 – December 3, 2026) lets Commerce bar importers whose imports of polysilicon products, including solar cells (8541.42) and modules (8541.43), run well above their historic averages, and caps weekly volumes for importers registered after August 6, 2026.

changes.title: Final AD/CVD determinations on solar cells from India, Indonesia and Laos
changes.detail: Commerce made final affirmative dumping and subsidy determinations on crystalline silicon solar cells and modules from India, Indonesia and Laos (investigations begun August 2025). Orders will issue only if the ITC makes final affirmative injury determinations.
changes.now: AD/CVD orders if the ITC finds injury

changes.title: Canada Section 338 duty now stacks on Section 232
changes.detail: Proclamation 11065 made the 50% duty on Canadian goods of the motor-vehicle list apply on top of Section 232 duties and changed the list: 8537.10.91 is now covered only for four statistical numbers (numerical controls, panel boards, programmable controllers and other boards). The other Chapter 85 lines stayed on the list.

changes.title: Section 232 duty on drones reaches drone docking stations
changes.detail: Proclamation 11055 imposed 100% on unmanned aircraft systems and their parts, including docking stations classified in 8504.40.95.80 and 8537.10.91.70 (note 43). UK goods pay +10% and goods of Japan, Korea, Taiwan, Switzerland, Liechtenstein and the EU 15% in total when substantially all critical components come from partner countries. Products on the Blue UAS lists start paying on February 9, 2027.

changes.title: 50% Section 338 duty on Canadian electronics and other goods
changes.detail: Proclamation 11048 imposed 50% on products of Canada in the note 51(b)(3) list to offset Canada's surtax on U.S. motor vehicles; Proclamation 11056 moved the start from August 19 to August 22, 2026. It covers 62 Chapter 85 lines, including smartphones, network gear, TVs, cameras, storage media and printed circuits, and is charged even when USMCA is claimed.

changes.title: Section 232 duty on solar cells and modules from December 4, 2026
changes.detail: Proclamation 11052 (signed August 6, 2026) sets, from December 4, 2026, a 15% Section 232 duty on polysilicon derivatives, including solar cells and modules, and minimum import prices: $0.22 per watt for cells and $0.38 per watt for modules. Entries without the importer's documentation pay the minimum price as a specific duty; others pay the shortfall below it. EU, Japanese, Korean, Taiwanese, Swiss and Liechtenstein products pay 15% in total, UK products 10%. It replaces the Section 201 safeguard that expired in February.

changes.title: Commerce proposes more metals derivatives, including insulated cable
changes.detail: Under the rolling inclusion authority of Proclamation 11021, Commerce asked for comments on adding derivative articles to the Section 232 metals duties, including insulated copper electric conductor cables of 8544.49 and 8544.60. Nothing has been added yet.

changes.title: UFLPA Entity List adds 43 entities
changes.detail: DHS added 43 entities to the UFLPA Entity List. Goods made wholly or in part by listed entities, or in Xinjiang, are presumed made with forced labor and are denied entry unless CBP grants an exception. Listed entities include polysilicon and transformer producers in Xinjiang.

changes.title: 2026 Section 301 tariffs on 60 economies: chips, phones and displays exempt
changes.detail: The 10% or 12.5% duties on goods of 60 economies (9903.05.20–9903.05.84) took effect on 909 Chapter 85 lines. Smartphones, switching apparatus, SSDs, display modules, monitors, semiconductors other than solar cells, and chips are exempt (note 52(b)); Section 232 goods and USMCA goods are exempt too. The EU, Japan, Korea and Taiwan pay a floor (10%–15% in place of a lower base rate).

changes.title: Section 122 surcharge expired
changes.detail: The 10% surcharge on products of all countries (9903.03.01) expired at the close of July 23, 2026. It had exempted smartphones, network switching gear, SSDs, display modules, monitors, semiconductors other than solar cells, chips and NdFeB magnets (note 2(aa)(ii)), Section 232 goods and USMCA goods.

changes.title: Section 301 tariff on Brazil
changes.detail: The 25% duty on goods of Brazil (9903.05.01) took effect, with the same electronics exemption list (note 50(a)(ii)) and Section 232 carve-out.

changes.title: Circumvention inquiry: solar cells finished in Ethiopia or Vietnam
changes.detail: Commerce opened a country-wide inquiry into whether solar cells completed in Ethiopia from Chinese parts, or assembled into modules in Vietnam with further Chinese inputs, circumvent the 2012 China solar orders.

changes.title: 2015 solar orders on China and Taiwan continued
changes.detail: After second sunset reviews, the 2015 antidumping orders on solar products from China and Taiwan and the countervailing order on China were continued.

changes.title: Proclamation 11032 adjusts the metals program
changes.detail: From June 8, 2026, metal content counts as U.S.-made when at least 85% was melted or smelted and cast in the United States (10%), parts used to make agricultural or industrial equipment pay 15% in total, and electric space heaters of 8516.29 moved to the 15% floor list.

changes.title: Taiwanese auto parts: 15% in total
changes.detail: Under the U.S.–Taiwan agreement, Taiwanese auto parts pay 15% in total, including the base rate, instead of 25% on top (9903.94.67).

changes.title: Section 232 metals duty moves to the full value
changes.detail: Proclamation 11021 rebuilt the aluminum, steel and copper program on the full customs value. Chapter 85 derivatives (motors, generating sets, transformers, appliance parts, insulated copper and aluminum cable) pay 25% (9903.82.09), and large transformers and some equipment parts a 15% floor through 2027 (9903.82.10). Before, listed derivatives paid 50% of their metal content. Manufacturing drawback is limited to trade-agreement partners.
changes.now: +25% on the full value (or a 15% floor)

changes.title: All IEEPA tariffs end; Section 122 surcharge begins
changes.detail: After the Supreme Court held on February 20, 2026 (Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump) that IEEPA does not authorize tariffs, Executive Order 14389 ended the Canada, Mexico, China and reciprocal duties, and CBP stopped collecting them from February 24, 2026. A 10% Section 122 surcharge (Proclamation 11012) applied from the same day until July 23, 2026, with the electronics exemptions of note 2(aa)(ii).

changes.title: Section 201 solar safeguard ends
changes.detail: The safeguard on crystalline silicon solar cells (above an annual quota) and modules, in place since February 7, 2018 and extended in 2022, terminated on February 6, 2026 (9903.45.21–9903.45.29 expired). The ITC is evaluating its effectiveness.
changes.before: Safeguard duty on cells above quota and on modules

changes.title: Section 232 semiconductor duty: computers only, not Chapter 85
changes.detail: Proclamation 11002 imposed 25% (9903.79.01) on semiconductor articles, defined in U.S. note 39(b) as goods of 8471.50, 8471.80 and 8473.30 that are or contain logic chips within narrow performance bands, with end-use exemptions (9903.79.03–.09). Chips, semiconductors and other Chapter 85 goods are not covered.

changes.title: China: lithium-ion batteries and permanent magnets to 25%
changes.detail: The second step of the 2024 review: lithium-ion batteries other than for EVs (8507.60) and permanent magnets (8505.11) went to 25% (9903.91.06). EV batteries had been raised to 25% on September 27, 2024.

changes.title: Section 301 tariff on Nicaragua phases in from 2027
changes.detail: Products of Nicaragua that are not CAFTA-DR originating goods will pay +10% from January 1, 2027 and +15% from January 1, 2028 (9903.89.01, U.S. note 29). The rate is 0% in 2026.

changes.title: Section 301 action on Chinese semiconductors: 0% now, increase June 23, 2027
changes.detail: USTR found China's targeting of the semiconductor industry actionable and imposed a tariff on Chinese semiconductors at 0%, rising on June 23, 2027 to a rate to be announced at least 30 days before. It adds to the 50% under note 31.

changes.title: 178 China Section 301 exclusions extended to November 9, 2026
changes.detail: USTR extended the 178 product exclusions (9903.88.69) through November 9, 2026. 26 Chapter 85 lines have an exclusion for specific described products (motors, power supplies, switches, relays, PCBs, cables).

changes.title: China IEEPA (fentanyl) duty cut to 10%
changes.detail: Executive Order 14357 cut the IEEPA duty on Chinese goods from 20% to 10%. Unlike the reciprocal tariff, it had no electronics exemption. Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: Section 232 on truck and bus parts; certified-parts elections
changes.detail: Proclamation 10984 imposed 25% on parts of medium- and heavy-duty vehicles (67 Chapter 85 lines, 9903.74.08) and let importers certify other parts for U.S. vehicle production or repair as Section 232 parts (9903.94.07, 9903.74.09 and partner headings). Korean auto parts moved to 15% in total on the same date (9903.94.63).

changes.title: Japanese auto parts: 15% in total
changes.detail: Japanese auto parts pay 15% in total, including the base rate (9903.94.43).

changes.title: More Chapter 85 goods become aluminum and steel derivatives
changes.detail: Commerce added 407 product codes to the Section 232 steel and aluminum derivatives, including generating sets, transformers, motors and insulated cable of Chapter 85, at 50% of the metal content. Proclamation 11021 replaced this with the full-value rates from April 6, 2026.

changes.title: EU auto parts: 15% in total
changes.detail: EU auto parts pay 15% in total, including the base rate (9903.94.53), retroactive to August 1, 2025.

changes.title: UK auto parts: 10% in total
changes.detail: UK auto parts on the note 33(j) list pay 10% in total (9903.94.32).

changes.title: AD/CVD orders on solar cells from Cambodia, Malaysia, Thailand and Vietnam
changes.detail: Commerce issued antidumping and countervailing duty orders on crystalline silicon solar cells and modules from Cambodia, Malaysia, Thailand and Vietnam.

changes.title: Aluminum wire and cable orders on China continued
changes.detail: After five-year reviews, Commerce continued the 2019 AD and CVD orders on aluminum wire and cable from China (8544.49.90, 8544.42.90). In January 2025 it found that cable completed in Vietnam and Korea from Chinese aluminum circumvents them.

changes.title: Section 232 duty on auto parts
changes.detail: Proclamation 10908 imposed 25% on parts of passenger vehicles and light trucks (9903.94.05), reaching 85 Chapter 85 lines, including batteries, motors, ignition and lighting equipment, car radios and wiring sets. USMCA parts and goods that are not such parts use 9903.94.06 (0%).

changes.title: Smartphones, chips and displays exempted from the reciprocal tariff
changes.detail: A presidential memorandum clarified that the 'semiconductors' exception of Executive Order 14257 covers 8471, 8473.30, 8486, smartphones (8517.13), 8517.62, SSDs (8523.51), display modules (8524), monitors (8528.52), most of 8541 and all of 8542, retroactive to April 5, 2025. The China and Canada/Mexico IEEPA duties still applied. All ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: IEEPA duties on China, Canada and Mexico
changes.detail: +20% on Chinese goods (10% from February 4, 2025, raised by Executive Order 14228) and +25% on goods of Canada and Mexico from March 4, 2025 (USMCA goods exempt from March 7, 2025). Ended February 24, 2026.

changes.title: China: semiconductors and chips to 50%
changes.detail: Semiconductors and chips of 8541 (other than solar cells) and 8542 moved from 25% (List 1) to 50% (9903.91.05).

changes.title: China: solar cells to 50%, EV batteries and battery parts to 25%
changes.detail: After the four-year review, Chinese solar cells and modules (8541.42/.43) went to 50% (9903.91.02), lithium-ion EV batteries (8507.60.00.10) and lead-acid battery parts (8507.90.40) to 25%.

changes.title: Large power transformer order on Korea continued
changes.detail: Commerce continued the 2012 antidumping order on large power transformers from Korea (8504.23, parts 8504.90).

changes.title: China solar orders reach cells and modules finished in Southeast Asia
changes.detail: Commerce found that solar cells and modules completed in Cambodia, Malaysia, Thailand and Vietnam from Chinese wafers or parts circumvent the 2012 China orders. Duties on such goods were waived until June 6, 2024 under a presidential emergency, if they were used in the United States.

changes.title: Russia: 35% in lieu of column 2
changes.detail: Proclamation 10420 set 35% in place of the column 2 rate on Russian goods of the note 30 list (18 Chapter 85 lines).

changes.title: Solar safeguard extended four years
changes.detail: Proclamation 10339 extended the Section 201 safeguard on solar cells and modules to February 6, 2026, with a larger tariff-rate quota for cells.

changes.title: China List 4A cut to 7.5%
changes.detail: The List 4A duty (9903.88.15) fell from 15% to 7.5%.

changes.title: AD/CVD orders on aluminum wire and cable from China
changes.detail: Commerce issued antidumping and countervailing duty orders on aluminum wire and cable from China.

changes.title: China List 4A
changes.detail: List 4A added 15% on more Chinese goods, including TVs, audio and many appliances.

changes.title: China List 3 raised to 25%
changes.detail: The List 3 duty rose from 10% to 25%.

changes.title: China List 3
changes.detail: List 3 added 10% on a broad range of Chinese goods.

changes.title: China List 2
changes.detail: List 2 added 25% on Chinese goods including some motors, batteries and semiconductors.

changes.title: China List 1
changes.detail: List 1 added 25% on Chinese goods including motors, transformers, capacitors, switches and semiconductors.

changes.title: Section 201 solar safeguard begins
changes.detail: Proclamation 9693 imposed a four-year safeguard on crystalline silicon solar cells above a quota and on modules.

changes.title: AD/CVD orders on solar products from China and Taiwan
changes.detail: Commerce issued antidumping orders on solar products from China and Taiwan and a countervailing order on China.

changes.title: AD/CVD orders on solar cells from China
changes.detail: Commerce issued antidumping and countervailing duty orders on crystalline silicon solar cells and modules from China.

changes.title: Antidumping order on large power transformers from Korea
changes.detail: Commerce issued an antidumping order on large power transformers from Korea.

changes.title: Antidumping order on small-diameter graphite electrodes from China
changes.detail: Commerce issued an antidumping order on small-diameter graphite electrodes from China (8545.11); it was continued again in September 2025.

understandIndustry.why:
U.S. imports of Chapter 85 electrical machinery and electronics were **$513.6B in 2025**, +5.7% from $485.9B in 2024. The five largest suppliers were Mexico ($91.4B), China ($84.0B), Vietnam ($61.9B), Taiwan ($37.0B), Thailand ($32.4B). By product group the largest were smartphones and network equipment (8517, $143.6B), integrated circuits (chips) (8542, $42.4B), insulated wire and cable, fiber-optic cable (8544, $36.9B), transformers, power supplies and inductors (8504, $35.4B); the largest six-digit lines were 8517.62 ($84.9B), 8517.13 ($52.4B), 8542.31 ($32.6B).

Most of these goods are exempt from the newest duties or pay little: smartphones, chips, semiconductors, SSDs, display modules and monitors are on the 2026 Section 301 exemption list, and USMCA goods from Mexico and Canada enter free of the 2026 duty. China, whose goods pay Section 301 duties on almost every line, shipped $84.0B (-34% on 2024). Mexico, whose USMCA-qualifying goods are exempt from the 2026 duty, shipped $91.4B. 

2025 is the latest full year of U.S. trade data. Duty-collected figures aren't available from an official source yet.

seo.title: Electronics Tariffs by Country: China, Mexico, Vietnam, Taiwan, Korea, Japan, Canada (HTS Ch. 85) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: The total U.S. tariff on Chapter 85 electrical goods by country and product: China 20%–62.5%, Vietnam and Thailand 12.5%, Malaysia and India 10%, Taiwan and Korea floors, Mexico and Canada Free with USMCA (Canada 50% on phones and TVs). Chips and smartphones explained.

industryAreas.intro:
Each cell is the base rate for that product group plus the extra duties for that country, minus any preference, from the current tariff schedule. Three patterns decide most cells. **Chips, semiconductors, smartphones, SSDs, display modules and monitors** are on the 2026 Section 301 exemption list, so they are Free from every country except China (50% on chips and semiconductors) and Canada (50% on phones and monitors). **Most other goods** pay their base rate plus the 2026 Section 301 duty: 10% (Mexico and Canada without USMCA, Malaysia, India, UK), 12.5% (Vietnam, Thailand), or a 10%–15% floor (EU, Japan, Korea, Taiwan); China adds 7.5% to 50% under its lists. **Section 232 goods** (auto parts, truck parts, metal-heavy transformers and cable) pay 25% (15% in total for the EU, Japan, Korea and Taiwan on auto parts) instead of the 2026 duty.

Cells with two figures depend on the use: a battery, motor or wiring set listed in U.S. note 33(g) pays the auto-parts duty only when it is a part of a car or light truck. The table does **not** include antidumping or countervailing duties (solar cells from China, Taiwan and Southeast Asia, aluminum wire and cable from China, large power transformers from Korea, graphite electrodes from China).

assumptions: Each total was computed by the official-measures calculator engine (the same data as the tariff calculator: measures.json, HTSUS 2026 Revision 21) for goods entered on 2026-10-13, priced on a $10,000 shipment and 1,000 units for per-unit rates.
Ranges like "Free · 11.8%" mean the group has lines with different base rates; select a cell to see which lines carry which rate.
Preferences: USMCA (S) is applied for Canada and Mexico on the "USMCA-qualifying" side; JP for Japan; KR for South Korea. GSP (A, A+) has lapsed and is not applied. Other preferences are not applied.
Conditional relief is not applied (it needs the importer's confirmation): 9903.88.69 (Section 301).
Any other country shows the range across every country not listed (column 2 countries — Cuba, North Korea, Russia, Belarus — aside), without preferences.

Cells with two or three figures depend on whether the goods are parts of cars or light trucks, or of trucks and buses (U.S. notes 33(g) and 38(i)); listed goods that are neither enter under 9903.94.06 or 9903.74.11 with no Section 232 duty. The certified-parts elections (9903.94.07, 9903.74.09) are optional and not applied.

Section 232 metals are shown at the default rates (25%, or the 15% floor). Lower rates for UK metal (15%), U.S.-melted metal (10%), parts for agricultural or industrial equipment (15% in total), articles under 15% metal by weight or with no metal (none) are not shown.

The IEEPA duties (9903.01.xx, 9903.02.xx) are still printed in the schedule but ended February 24, 2026; the Section 122 surcharge (9903.03.01) expired July 23, 2026; and the Section 201 solar safeguard (9903.45.21–.29) ended February 6, 2026. None is applied. The Section 232 polysilicon duty on solar cells and modules (from December 4, 2026) is not yet in effect.

Antidumping and countervailing duties are not included: solar cells and modules (China, Taiwan, Cambodia, Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam), aluminum wire and cable (China), large power transformers (Korea) and small-diameter graphite electrodes (China).

Entry rules: FCC equipment authorization for radio-frequency devices, DOE energy-conservation certification for regulated motors, transformers and appliances, FDA radiation-safety rules for microwave ovens and lasers, hazmat rules for lithium batteries, and UFLPA screening (see Import documents).
industryAreas.exemptionCheck: Read U.S. notes 2(aa), 16, 18, 19, 20, 29, 30, 31, 33, 38, 39, 43, 50, 51 and 52 to Chapter 99 subchapter III in the 2026 Revision 21. Note 52(f) and 50(a)(vi) exclude Section 232 metals, auto and truck parts. Note 39(b) limits the semiconductor duty to 8471.50, 8471.80 and 8473.30. Note 33(g) lists the auto-part subheadings of 8501, 8507, 8511, 8512, 8519, 8525, 8527, 8536, 8537, 8539 and 8544.30; note 38(i) the truck-part lines; note 16(c)(vi)–(x) the metals lines; note 51(b)(3) the Canada lines; note 43(c) the drone docking stations; note 30 the Russia 35% lines; note 18 (solar safeguard) has expired. tariffEngineering.h1: HTS Chapter 85: Electrical Machinery & Electronics — Import Documents & Ways to Lower Duty

seo.title: Importing Electronics, Batteries & Solar: FCC, DOE, UFLPA, Section 232 Rules & Ways to Lower Duty (HTS Ch. 85) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: The rules for each HTS Chapter 85 line: FCC equipment authorization, DOE energy certification, FDA radiation rules, lithium battery hazmat, UFLPA polysilicon tracing, Section 232 and Section 301 entry headings, AD/CVD, plus legal ways to pay less: USMCA, not-a-vehicle-part, metals relief, exclusions, classification and Chapter 98.

tariffEngineering.intro:
Most Chapter 85 goods need an agency clearance as well as the right tariff headings. Radio-frequency devices need **FCC equipment authorization**, and equipment of Covered List companies (and, from October 13, 2026, devices with their logic components) cannot be authorized. Regulated motors, transformers, power supplies, lamps and water heaters need **DOE certification**; microwave ovens and other radiation-emitting products follow **FDA** standards; lithium batteries are **hazardous materials** in transport; and solar products face **UFLPA** forced-labor screening that traces polysilicon to its source.

The legal ways to pay less depend on the product: USMCA origin, documenting that a listed battery or motor is not a vehicle part, the Section 232 metals relief headings, the remaining China exclusions, exact classification into the exempt electronics subheadings, the informational-materials and civil-aircraft reliefs, Chapter 98 for U.S. components and drawback. Each rule and lever links to its regulation or proclamation.

levers.title: Qualify the goods for USMCA (Mexico, Canada)
levers.saves: The base rate, the 10% 2026 Section 301 duty and the Section 232 auto-parts and truck-parts duties (9903.94.06, 9903.74.10)
levers.appliesTo: Goods of Mexico and Canada that meet the USMCA rules of origin
levers.document: A USMCA certification of origin from the importer, exporter or producer, with records supporting the tariff-shift or regional value content rule.
levers.caveat: USMCA does not lift the Section 232 metals duty (insulated cable, transformers) or Canada's 50% Section 338 duty on smartphones, network gear, TVs and the other note 51(b)(3) lines.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 33(h), 38, 52(g)–(h)

levers.title: Document that listed goods are not vehicle parts
levers.saves: The 25% Section 232 auto-parts duty (or the 15% partner rate): note 33(h)(ii) sends listed goods that are not parts of cars or light trucks to 9903.94.06 at 0%
levers.appliesTo: The 85 lines on the note 33(g) list: motors (8501.32–.52), lead-acid and lithium-ion batteries (8507.10, 8507.60), ignition and lighting, car audio, boards (8537.10/.20), wiring sets (8544.30)
levers.document: Evidence of the goods' design and use: specifications, the buyer and the application (for example energy-storage or consumer-device batteries). CBP may ask for it.
levers.caveat: CBP's CSMS # 64916652 repeats the HTS rule but CBP has not published how it decides whether a multi-use article (a lithium-ion cell, a motor) is a vehicle part, so whether end use or design governs is unconfirmed. Without the 232 duty, the 2026 Section 301 duty applies instead.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 33(g)–(h)

levers.title: Elect the Section 232 auto-part treatment where it is cheaper
levers.saves: For EU, Japanese, Korean and Taiwanese parts on the metals list, 15% in total instead of the base rate plus 25%
levers.appliesTo: Parts not on the note 33(g) or 38(i) lists, used for U.S. vehicle production or repair
levers.document: The importer of record's certification that the parts are for automobile (or truck) production or repair in the United States (headings 9903.94.07, 9903.94.45/.55/.65/.69, 9903.74.09).
levers.caveat: Optional and binding for the entry: elsewhere it usually raises the duty to 25%. Not available for Chapter 72, 73 or 76 goods.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 33(p), 33(r), 38(j)

levers.title: Use the Section 232 metals relief headings
levers.saves: All or part of the 25% (or 15% floor) metals duty
levers.appliesTo: The 83 Chapter 85 lines on the metals lists (transformers, large motors, generating sets, insulated cable, appliance parts)
levers.document: Bills of materials and weights: no aluminum, steel or copper (9903.82.01, none); metals under 15% of the weight (9903.82.03, none); at least 85% U.S.-melted or smelted and cast metal (9903.82.06, 10%); UK goods with 95% UK metal (9903.82.05, 15%); parts for agricultural or industrial equipment (9903.82.25, 15% in total until 2027); motorcycle parts for U.S. manufacturing (9903.82.13, none).
levers.caveat: Each is a claim the importer must support with mill and supplier records; Russia, Belarus, Cuba and North Korea cannot use most of them.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 16

levers.title: Classify precisely: the electronics exemptions are by subheading
levers.saves: The 2026 Section 301 duty (10%–12.5%) and the Brazil duty on goods that belong in an exempt subheading
levers.appliesTo: Borderline goods: display modules (8524, exempt) versus parts (8529); switching and routing apparatus (8517.62, exempt) versus other network apparatus (8517.69); ICs and multi-component ICs (8542) versus modules of 8543 or 8473
levers.document: Technical data supporting the classification; for certainty, a binding CBP ruling.
levers.caveat: Only the correct classification counts: chapter notes 7 and 12 set the precedence of 8524, 8541 and 8542. Misclassification risks penalties.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 52(b)

levers.title: Claim a China Section 301 exclusion
levers.saves: The China list duty (25% or 7.5%) on the excluded product
levers.appliesTo: 26 Chapter 85 lines with a product-specific exclusion (motors, power supplies, switches, PCBs, cables) until November 9, 2026
levers.document: Report 9903.88.69 with the Chapter 85 line; the goods must match the exclusion's product description exactly.
levers.caveat: Expires November 9, 2026 unless USTR extends it again; the 12.5% 2026 duty is not excluded.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 20(vvv)

levers.title: Recorded informational materials
levers.saves: The 2026 Section 301 duty (9903.05.92) and the Brazil duty (9903.05.09)
levers.appliesTo: Discs, tapes and other media of 8523.29, 8523.41, 8523.49 and 8523.80.10 carrying films, recordings or other informational content
levers.document: Description of the recorded content (films, recordings, publications).
levers.caveat: Does not lift the China list duties (List 4A on most media) or Canada's Section 338 duty.

citations.label: HTSUS Ch. 99, subch. III, U.S. note 52
USTR notice of Section 301 actions on 60 economies (91 FR 47318)

levers.title: Know the country of origin before you buy
levers.saves: The China rates (up to 62.5%) when the goods are genuinely made elsewhere
levers.appliesTo: All lines, especially chips, solar cells and modules, batteries and cable
levers.document: Production records showing where the article was substantially transformed (for example where the chip was fabricated, the cell made or the cable drawn and insulated).
levers.caveat: Simple assembly or packaging in a third country does not change origin, and Commerce has found solar modules and aluminum cable finished in Southeast Asia to circumvent the China AD/CVD orders.

levers.title: U.S. components assembled abroad (Chapter 98)
levers.saves: Duty on the value of U.S.-made components
levers.appliesTo: Electronics assembled abroad from U.S.-made fabricated components (for example U.S. chips or boards)
levers.document: Foreign assembler's declaration and importer's endorsement showing the U.S. components and their value.
levers.caveat: The 2026 Section 301 duty is charged on the value less the U.S. components; Section 232 goods entered under 9802.00.60 pay on the full value.

provisions.rate: Duty on the full value less the cost or value of U.S. components
provisions.text: Articles assembled abroad from fabricated components, the product of the United States

finalConclusion.h1: HTS Chapter 85: Electrical Machinery & Electronics — Tariff FAQ

seo.title: Electronics Tariffs FAQ: Are Electronics Exempt? Semiconductors, Smartphones, Batteries, Solar Panels (HTS Ch. 85) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: Answers to what people search about U.S. tariffs on HTS Chapter 85 goods: whether electronics are exempt, the tariff on semiconductors, smartphones and iPhones, lithium-ion batteries, solar panels, copper wire, transformers and motors, by country, with HS codes.

finalConclusion.intro: Straight answers to the most-searched questions about U.S. tariffs on electrical machinery and electronics (HTS Chapter 85), by product, by country and by HS code. Each answer links to the page with the detail and the official sources.
keyTakeaways: Base rates are low (566 of 982 lines Free); the extra duties decide the cost. Smartphones, chips, semiconductors, SSDs, display modules and monitors are Free from every country except China (50% on chips and semiconductors) and Canada (50% on phones and monitors).

China pays Section 301 on almost every line: 25% or 7.5% under the 2018–2019 lists, 50% on chips, semiconductors and solar cells, 25% on lithium-ion batteries and permanent magnets, plus 12.5% on most lines since July 24, 2026.

Other countries pay the 2026 Section 301 duty (10% or 12.5%; a 10%–15% floor for the EU, Japan, Korea and Taiwan) on most goods; USMCA goods of Mexico and Canada are exempt. Section 232 adds 25% on auto parts (when they are car parts), truck parts and metal-heavy goods such as insulated cable and transformers.

The IEEPA tariffs ended February 24, 2026, the Section 122 surcharge July 23, 2026 and the solar safeguard February 6, 2026. A Section 232 duty on solar cells and modules starts December 4, 2026. AD/CVD on solar, aluminum cable, transformers and graphite electrodes comes on top.
In 2025 the U.S. imported $513.6B of Chapter 85 goods, Mexico ($91.4B) and China ($84.0B) first.

faqs.question: What is HTS Chapter 85?
faqs.answer: Chapter 85 of the Harmonized Tariff Schedule covers electrical machinery and equipment and their parts: motors, generators and transformers, batteries, household appliances, smartphones and network equipment, audio and video apparatus, cameras, TVs and monitors, switches and connectors, lamps and LEDs, semiconductors, solar cells, integrated circuits, insulated wire and cable, and e-waste. The current edition (2026 Revision 21) has 982 ten-digit lines in 48 headings (8501–8549).

faqs.question: Are electronics exempt from tariffs?
searchedAs: are electronics still exempt from tariffs
are electronic components exempt from tariffs
are electronics exempt from us tariffs
faqs.answer: Partly. Smartphones (8517.13), switching and routing apparatus (8517.62), SSDs (8523.51), flat panel display modules (8524), computer monitors (8528.52), semiconductor devices other than solar cells (8541), chips (8542) and NdFeB magnets are exempt from the 2026 Section 301 duties (note 52(b)); most of them were also exempt from the 2025 reciprocal tariff. They are not exempt from China's Section 301 duties (50% on chips and semiconductors) or Canada's 50% Section 338 duty on phones and monitors. Other electronics, such as TVs, audio equipment, cameras, batteries and components, pay the 2026 duty (10%–12.5%) and, from China, Section 301.

faqs.question: What is the U.S. tariff on semiconductors from China?
faqs.answer: 50% on top of the base rate (Free) for Chinese semiconductors and chips of 8541 and 8542 (other than solar cells), under Section 301 heading 9903.91.05 since January 1, 2025. The 12.5% 2026 Section 301 duty does not apply to them. A separate Section 301 action on Chinese semiconductors is at 0% until June 23, 2027, when it rises to a rate USTR will announce. Chips from Taiwan, Korea, Malaysia, Vietnam and other countries pay no duty.

faqs.question: Is there a Section 232 or 100% tariff on semiconductors?
faqs.answer: No 100% tariff is in force. Proclamation 11002 imposed a 25% Section 232 duty (9903.79.01) from January 15, 2026, but U.S. note 39 limits it to goods of 8471.50, 8471.80 and 8473.30 (computers and computer parts) that are or contain logic chips within narrow performance bands, with exemptions for U.S. data centers, repairs, R&D, startups, consumer, industrial and public-sector uses. Chips and semiconductors imported on their own (8541, 8542) are not covered, so Taiwanese chips enter free.

faqs.question: Is there a tariff on smartphones and iPhones?
searchedAs: is there a tariff on iphones
faqs.answer: Smartphones (8517.13.00.00) enter free from China, India, Vietnam and almost every other country: the base rate is Free, smartphones are on no China Section 301 list, and they are exempt from the 2026 Section 301 duties (note 52(b)). The IEEPA duties that applied to Chinese phones in 2025 ended on February 24, 2026. The exception is Canada: Canadian smartphones pay 50% under Section 338 since August 22, 2026.

faqs.question: What is the tariff on lithium-ion batteries from China?
searchedAs: tariffs on lithium ion batteries from china
tariff on lithium batteries from china
what is the current tariff on batteries from china
us tariffs on batteries from china
faqs.answer: 40.9% for lithium-ion batteries of 8507.60 that are not car parts: 3.4% base, 25% Section 301 (9903.91.06, since January 1, 2026) and 12.5% (2026 Section 301). Batteries that are parts of passenger cars or light trucks, such as EV battery packs, pay 53.4%: 3.4% + 25% Section 301 + 25% Section 232 auto parts (the 12.5% does not apply). CBP has not published how it treats batteries whose use in vehicles is mixed or unknown. Lead-acid batteries from China pay about 41%. From Mexico or Canada, USMCA batteries enter free.

faqs.question: What are the U.S. tariffs on solar panels in 2026?
searchedAs: tariff on solar panels from china
us tariff on solar panels from india
tariffs on solar panels from india
faqs.answer: Solar cells and modules (8541.42, 8541.43) are Free at base. Chinese ones pay 62.5% (50% + 12.5% Section 301) plus AD/CVD; Vietnamese, Thai, Malaysian and Cambodian ones pay 10%–12.5% plus the 2025 AD/CVD orders; Indian ones 10%, with AD/CVD orders to follow if the ITC finds injury. The Section 201 safeguard ended February 6, 2026. From December 4, 2026, Section 232 adds 15% (15% in total for the EU, Japan, Korea and Taiwan) and minimum import prices of $0.22 per watt for cells and $0.38 for modules.

faqs.question: What is the tariff on electronics from China?
searchedAs: tariff on electronics from china to usa
faqs.answer: It depends on the product: smartphones Free; chips and semiconductors 50%; solar cells 62.5%; lithium-ion batteries 40.9% (53.4% as car parts); TVs about 24% (base + 7.5% List 4A + 12.5%); modems, switches and routers 25% (8517.62.00.10/.20, List 3); and most components, motors and transformers 37.5% plus the base rate (25% List 1–3 + 12.5%). Section 232 duties stack on top for auto parts and metal-heavy goods.

faqs.question: What is the tariff on electronics from Canada, Japan, India, Germany or Taiwan?
faqs.answer: Phones, chips, SSDs, display modules and monitors are Free from all of them except Canada (50% on phones, network gear, TVs and monitors under Section 338). Other goods pay the 2026 Section 301 duty: India and the UK +10%; Japan, Korea and Taiwan 12.5%, 12.5% and 10% in place of a lower base rate; Germany and the EU 10% in place of a lower base rate; USMCA goods of Canada are exempt. Auto parts pay 15% in total from Japan, the EU, Korea and Taiwan, 25% from India.

faqs.question: Is there a tariff on copper wire and cable?
searchedAs: is there a tariff on copper wire
faqs.answer: Yes. Insulated copper wire and cable of 8544.42 and 8544.49.10, and insulated cable of 8544.19, 8544.49.20/.90 and 8544.60, pay a 25% Section 232 duty on the full value (9903.82.09) from every country since April 6, 2026, on top of the base rate and even with a USMCA claim. Cable whose metal is under 15% of its weight is exempt. Bare copper wire of Chapter 74 pays 50%. Chinese aluminum wire and cable also carries AD/CVD.

faqs.question: What is the U.S. tariff on transformers?
faqs.answer: Liquid-dielectric and other transformers up to 10,000 kVA pay their base rate (Free to 6.6%) plus 25% Section 232 on the full value; transformers over 10,000 kVA and other transformers over 500 kVA pay 15% in total through 2027, then the base rate plus 25%. Chinese transformers also pay 25% Section 301. Large power transformers from Korea carry an antidumping order.

faqs.question: What is the tariff on electric motors?
faqs.answer: Motors of 8501 have base rates of Free to 6.7%. Motors of 8501.32–8501.52 pay 25% Section 232 when they are parts of cars or light trucks (15% in total from the EU, Japan, Korea and Taiwan) and 25% when they are truck parts; some multi-phase AC motors over 75 kW (8501.53.60, 8501.53.80) pay 25% under the metals program. Otherwise the 2026 Section 301 duty applies (10%–12.5%). Chinese motors pay 25% Section 301 plus 12.5% or the Section 232 duty.

faqs.question: What is the tariff on TVs?
faqs.answer: LCD and OLED TVs of 8528.72 have base rates of Free to 5%. A 65-inch TV (8528.72.64.60, 3.9%) pays 23.9% from China, 16.4% from Vietnam or Thailand, 13.9% from a non-USMCA Mexican factory and nothing from a USMCA-qualifying one; Canadian TVs pay 50% more under Section 338.

faqs.question: What are the HS codes for smartphones, chips, batteries, solar panels and cable?
faqs.answer: Smartphones 8517.13; routers, switches and modems 8517.62; processors and controllers 8542.31, memories 8542.32; lithium-ion batteries 8507.60 (8507.60.00.10 for EV batteries); solar cells 8541.42 and modules 8541.43; insulated cable fitted with connectors 8544.42 and other cable up to 1,000 V 8544.49. Use the searchable rate table on the overview to find the 10-digit line and its rates.

faqs.question: Where does the U.S. import electronics and electrical equipment from?
searchedAs: where does the us import electronics from
where does the us get semiconductors
does the us get semiconductors from taiwan
faqs.answer: In 2025 U.S. imports of Chapter 85 goods were $513.6B (+5.7% on 2024). The largest suppliers were Mexico ($91.4B), China ($84.0B), Vietnam ($61.9B), Taiwan ($37.0B), Thailand ($32.4B). The largest product groups were smartphones and network equipment (8517, $143.6B), integrated circuits (chips) (8542, $42.4B), insulated wire and cable, fiber-optic cable (8544, $36.9B), transformers, power supplies and inductors (8504, $35.4B). Integrated circuits (8542, $42.4B) came mostly from Taiwan ($13.0B), Malaysia ($10.7B), Israel ($4.42B), Costa Rica ($2.37B).
